intro_en: Using the て-form from Lesson 14, in this lesson you will learn to ask permission ("may I do this?") and to state a prohibition ("you must not do this here"). You will also see how the same ています form shows not only "I am doing" but also states and habits, such as "I live in Chennai", "I work at a bank" and "I know him".

g15-1.explanation_en: To ask permission, add も いいですか after the て-form: 写真を撮ってもいいですか = "May I take a photo?". The literal meaning is "even if I take (撮っても), is it all right (いいですか)?". It is equivalent to the Tamil ending "may I" (-லாமா, as in எடுக்கலாமா?, may I take?). To give permission, say ええ、いいですよ or はい、どうぞ. To refuse, the Japanese custom is to say すみません、ちょっと… softly and leave it unfinished, or more directly いいえ、〜てはいけません (g15-2). Use the full form with も, 撮ってもいいですか. You will also hear 撮っていいですか in casual speech, but the JLPT tests the form with も. Without the question, 〜てもいいです means "you may do it", which gives permission.
g15-1.tamil_parallel_en: இங்கே உட்காரலாமா? ("May I sit here?") = ここに座ってもいいですか. 座って matches Tamil உட்கார்ந்து ("having sat"), and も いい means -ஆலும் சரி ("even if, it's fine"), which together work like Tamil -லாம் ("may").
g15-1.formation_en:
V て-form + も + いいですか (asking permission)
V て-form + も + いいです (giving permission)
Answer: ええ、いいですよ。/ はい、どうぞ。/ すみません、ちょっと…。
g15-1.pitfalls_en: Forgetting も in てもいい is a common mistake. When asking permission, don't confuse it with 〜ましょうか ("shall I do it?", an offer of help); 〜てもいいですか means "am I allowed?".

g15-2.explanation_en: To state a prohibition, add は いけません after the て-form: ここでたばこを吸ってはいけません = "You must not smoke here". The literal meaning is "if you smoke (吸っては), it won't do (いけません)". It is equivalent to the Tamil ending "must not" (-க் கூடாது, as in பிடிக்கக் கூடாது, must not smoke, or செய்யக் கூடாது, must not do). It is a very firm prohibition, used in rules, notices, by teachers to students and by parents to children. We don't say it directly to a superior. It is the firm "no" answer to a 〜てもいいですか question: いいえ、〜てはいけません. Here, pronounce は as "wa".
g15-2.tamil_parallel_en: இங்கே புகை பிடிக்கக் கூடாது ("You must not smoke here") = ここでたばこを吸ってはいけません. 吸っては matches Tamil பிடித்தால் ("if you smoke"), and いけません matches ஆகாது ("won't do"), like Tamil -க் கூடாது.
g15-2.formation_en:
V て-form + は + いけません
吸います → 吸って + はいけません; 入ります → 入って + はいけません; 使います → 使って + はいけません
Question and answer: 〜てもいいですか。— いいえ、〜てはいけません。
g15-2.pitfalls_en: Using も, as in 吸ってもいけません, is wrong: prohibition takes は, permission takes も. Because this is a strict prohibition, don't say it directly to older people.

g15-3.explanation_en: In Lesson 14 you learned ています as "an action happening now". But with some verbs, ています shows a "state" that continues as the result of an action. 住んでいます = "I live" (I moved there once and I am still there); 持っています = "I have / I own"; 知っています = "I know" (I learned it once and still know it); 立っています / 座っています = "is standing / is sitting". 結婚しています ("is married") is the same type (you will study this word fully later). It is just like Tamil expressing a state with a verbal participle + "be" (இரு, as in உட்கார்ந்திருக்கிறார், is seated, and தெரிந்திருக்கிறது, is known). With these verbs, the ます-form (住みます、持ちます) means "will do from now on"; for a current state, always use ています.
g15-3.tamil_parallel_en: நான் சென்னையில் வசிக்கிறேன் ("I live in Chennai") = チェンナイに住んでいます; என்னிடம் குடை இருக்கிறது ("I have an umbrella") = 傘を持っています. Tamil verbal participle + இரு ("be") matches Japanese て + います.
g15-3.formation_en:
V て-form + います (state)
住みます → 住んでいます; 持ちます → 持っています; 知ります → 知っています; 座ります → 座っています; 立ちます → 立っています
Negative: 〜ていません (exception: 知っています → 知りません, g15-5)
g15-3.pitfalls_en: If you say "I live in Chennai" as チェンナイに住みます, the meaning changes to "I am going to live there from now on". "I have a car" = 車を持っています (or 車があります).

g15-4.explanation_en: ています does a third job too: it describes a long-running habit or a person's occupation. 兄は銀行で働いています = "My older brother works at a bank". This does not mean he is working at this very moment; it is his job. あの店で切符を売っています = "They sell tickets at that shop" (regularly). Just as Tamil states a job in the present tense, as in "he teaches English at a school" (அவர் பள்ளியில் ஆங்கிலம் கற்பிக்கிறார்), Japanese uses ています. To ask "what do you do (for work)?", say お仕事は何ですか or 何をしていますか. You have to tell from context whether it means "happening now" (g14-4) or "habit": with 今 it is now; with 毎日 or an occupation, it is a habit.
g15-4.tamil_parallel_en: அண்ணன் வங்கியில் வேலை செய்கிறார் ("My older brother works at a bank", as his job) = 兄は銀行で働いています. Tamil uses the simple present for an occupation; Japanese uses ています.
g15-4.formation_en:
N (place) + で + V て-form + います (occupation / habit)
働きます → 働いています; 売ります → 売っています; 教えます → 教えています; 作ります → 作っています; 勉強します → 勉強しています
g15-4.pitfalls_en: When stating someone's job, if you use the ます-form, as in 銀行で働きます, it sounds like "will work (future)"; 働いています is the natural form.

g15-5.explanation_en: "I know" = 知っています (a state, g15-3). But "I don't know" is not 知っていません; we say 知りません. This is an important exception. The reason: since the act of "getting to know" never happened, negating "I am in the state of knowing" doesn't make sense. Tamil also simply says "I know" (தெரியும்) / "I don't know" (தெரியாது); we don't say "was not known" (தெரிந்திருக்கவில்லை). 知っています means knowing a person, a place or a piece of information; 分かります (Lesson 9) means understanding a language or a meaning: 日本語が分かります (புரியும், "I understand"), 田中さんを知っています (தெரியும், "I know").
g15-5.tamil_parallel_en: தெரியுமா? — தெரியும் / தெரியாது ("Do you know? — I know / I don't know") = 知っていますか。— 知っています / 知りません. Like Tamil தெரியாது, the Japanese negative is a simple form, 知りません.
g15-5.formation_en:
Question: N を 知っていますか
Yes: はい、知っています
No: いいえ、知りません (not 知っていません)
g15-5.pitfalls_en: 知っていません is a mistake Tamil speakers (and all learners) often make; always say 知りません. Use 知っています only in a "yes" answer.

g15-6.explanation_en: 住む (to live) and 勤める (to work for a company) both take に for the place, not で: 東京に住んでいます、銀行に勤めています. The reason: they describe a state of "being at / belonging to" a place, like あります / います (Lesson 10, に). But 働く (to work) marks the place where an action happens, so it takes で: 銀行で働いています. In Tamil both use the same ending (-இல், as in வங்கியில், at the bank), so you need to remember this difference carefully: 勤める・住む → に, 働く → で. To ask: どこに住んでいますか / どこに勤めていますか.
g15-6.tamil_parallel_en: நான் மதுரையில் வசிக்கிறேன் ("I live in Madurai") = マドゥライに住んでいます; அக்கா வங்கியில் பணிபுரிகிறார் ("My older sister works for a bank") = 姉は銀行に勤めています. Here Tamil -இல் becomes に, not で.
g15-6.formation_en:
N (place) + に + 住んでいます
N (company) + に + 勤めています
(compare: N (place) + で + 働いています)
Question: どこに 住んでいますか / どこに 勤めていますか
g15-6.pitfalls_en: Using で, as in 東京で住んでいます or 銀行で勤めています, is a mistake Tamil speakers make very often. Don't always translate the Tamil ending "in / at" (-இல்) as で.

items.L15-q01: 切符 = きっぷ (டிக்கெட், ticket). きっふ is a mistake with ぷ changed to ふ; don't confuse it with 切手 (きって, stamp).
items.L15-q02: 入口 = いりぐち (நுழைவாயில், entrance). Guessing はいりぐち from the verb 入る (はいる) is wrong; いりくち changes ぐ to く.
items.L15-q03: 仕事 = しごと (வேலை, work). しこと is a mistake with ご changed to こ.
items.L15-q04: でぐち = 出口 (வெளியேறும் வழி, exit), from 出 (out) + 口 (mouth / way). 山口 is a look-alike place name.
items.L15-q05: To live = 住む → 住んで (வசித்து, living). 往, 注 and 柱 are look-alike characters that all contain the part 主.
items.L15-q06: A no-smoking room won't have an ashtray = 灰皿 (சாம்பல் தட்டு, ashtray). The others have nothing to do with smoking.
items.L15-q07: What a camera needs is film = フィルム (ஃபிலிம், film). マッチ (தீப்பெட்டி, matches) has nothing to do with cameras.
items.L15-q08: "Works for a bank" = 銀行に勤めています (வங்கியில் பணிபுரிகிறார்). 住んで (வசிக்கிறார், lives) doesn't fit with a bank.
items.L15-q09: "Please sit" on a chair = 座ってください (உட்காருங்கள், please sit). 立って (நில்லுங்கள், stand) doesn't fit with a chair.
items.L15-q10: The shop "sells" vegetables and fruit = 売っています (விற்கிறது, sells). 吸って (புகை பிடித்து, smoking) doesn't fit.
items.L15-q11: "I leave the house" = 家を出ます (வீட்டிலிருந்து புறப்படுகிறேன்). For 入ります (நுழைகிறேன், enter), it would be 家に入ります with に.
items.L15-q12: 銀行に勤めています = 銀行で働いています (வங்கியில் வேலை செய்கிறார், works at a bank). 銀行へ行きます means going there once, not an occupation.
items.L15-q13: Teaches English at a school = a teacher (先生, ஆசிரியர்). 学生 is the one who learns, the opposite side.
items.L15-q14: 持っていますか (வைத்திருக்கிறீர்களா?, do you have it?) = ありますか (இருக்கிறதா?, is there one?). 買いましたか (வாங்கினீர்களா?, did you buy it?) has a different meaning.
items.L15-q15: To ask permission, use て-form + も + いいですか: 撮ってもいいですか (எடுக்கலாமா?, may I take a photo?). 撮っては is for prohibition (with いけません).
items.L15-q16: Prohibition = て + は + いけません (கூடாது, must not). Don't confuse it with も (permission).
items.L15-q17: "I don't know" = 知りません (தெரியாது). 知っていません is a wrong form; this is the key exception in this lesson.
items.L15-q18: The place for 住む (வசிக்க, to live) takes に: 東京に住んでいます. で is the mistake of thinking of the Tamil ending "in / at" (-இல்).
items.L15-q19: The place where 働く (வேலை செய், to work) happens takes で. With 勤める it is に (病院に勤めています); choose by looking at the verb.
items.L15-q20: The answer is 持っていません, so the question is about a state: 持っていますか (வைத்திருக்கிறீர்களா?, do you have it?). 持ちますか would mean "will you hold it?" (future).
items.L15-q21: Where you live now is a state = 住んでいますか (வசிக்கிறீர்களா?, do you live?). 住みますか would change the meaning to "where will you live from now on?".
items.L15-q22: 写真を → 撮っても → いいですか (புகைப்படம் எடுக்கலாமா?, may I take a photo?). To ask permission: て + も + いいですか.
items.L15-q23: 駅の近くの (ஸ்டேஷன் அருகிலுள்ள, near the station) → 銀行に → 勤めています. The place for 勤める takes に.
items.L15-q24: この部屋で → たばこを → 吸っては → いけません (புகை பிடிக்கக் கூடாது, must not smoke). Prohibition = て + は + いけません.
items.L15-q25: [1] 住みます: み → んで → 住んでいます (வசிக்கிறேன், live; a state). [2] Prohibition = 吸ってはいけません (புகை பிடிக்கக் கூடாது); 吸っても would be permission. [3] "I don't know" = 知りません (தெரியாது); 知っていません is wrong.
